brief: 5 prompt frameworks every AI builder needs in 2026 — with examples.

slots.postLine: every AI builder needs in their stack
slots.cardText: This stencil-stamp guide covers RTF, CoT, RAG, ToT and meta-prompting with copy-paste examples.

slots.toolTagline: Five battle-tested patterns for reliable AI output.
slots.bodyText: These five frameworks form the foundation of modern prompt engineering. Master them to build predictable AI systems.
slots.feat1Sub: Define role, task and format to shape every response.
slots.feat2Sub: Force step-by-step reasoning before the model answers.
slots.feat3Sub: Inject external data without losing instruction fidelity.

slots.toolTagline: The simplest way to eliminate ambiguity in any prompt.
slots.bodyText: RTF anchors prompts with three anchors: who the AI is, what it must do, and how to deliver. Example: "Act as a security auditor. Scan this code. Output markdown."
slots.feat1Sub: Set expertise level and persona to shape tone and depth.
slots.feat2Sub: Request JSON, markdown or tables to parse output instantly.
slots.feat3Sub: Add constraints like word count to reduce drift.

slots.toolTagline: Force the model to think out loud before it commits to an answer.
slots.bodyText: Append "Let's work through this step by step" to reduce logic errors by up to 40%. Example: "Solve this bug. Explain your reasoning before giving the fix."
slots.feat1Text: FORCE IT TO THINK OUT LOUD
slots.feat1Sub: Require reasoning first so errors surface early in the chain.
slots.feat2Sub: Ask the model to review its own steps for contradictions.
slots.feat3Sub: Provide worked examples to standardize the reasoning style.

slots.toolTagline: Inject external knowledge without polluting your system instructions.
slots.bodyText: Wrap documents in <context> tags and separate them from the user query. Example: "Using only the API docs below, generate the curl command."
slots.feat1Sub: Use XML or markdown blocks to isolate context from instructions.
slots.feat2Sub: Require page or line references to hallucinate less.
slots.feat3Sub: Feed only the most relevant chunks to stay inside context windows.

slots.toolTagline: Let the model explore multiple reasoning paths before choosing one.
slots.bodyText: Ask the model to generate three approaches, evaluate each, then execute the winner. Example: "Propose 3 architectures. Score them for latency and cost, then build the best."
slots.feat1Sub: Force multiple solution branches to escape local reasoning maxima.
slots.feat2Sub: Apply explicit criteria to kill weak paths early.
slots.feat3Sub: Allow the agent to retry from a previous node on failure.

slots.toolTagline: Build prompts that write, test and refine other prompts automatically.
slots.bodyText: Use a meta-prompt to generate task-specific prompts from raw goals. Example: "Create a prompt that turns customer complaints into JIRA tickets with severity labels."
slots.feat1Sub: Store reusable meta-prompts in your codebase for team consistency.
slots.feat2Sub: Generate evaluation criteria and run against sample inputs.
slots.feat3Sub: Track prompt diffs in git to measure output drift over time.

slots.ctaBody: Bookmark this carousel and share it with your team. Which framework will you deploy first? Drop a comment below.
